source: NC State Extension Gardener Plant Toolbox
description: Air plant is a small, evergreen, epiphytic herbaceous perennial from Mexico and Central America. It is a member of the pineapple family (Bromeliaceae). The species epithet means "violet flower" and describes the most common color of the flower of the wild-type species. Air plant is a popular bromeliad that is an epiphyte or lithophyte in nature, so it is well adapted to growing on various wood, ceramic, or glass mounts. They should not be planted in soil but can be placed in pots or mounted on objects. They require high humidity, and the silvery scales on the leaves are able to capture some moisture from the air. Nevertheless, they need regular, thorough watering. Be sure to gently shake any excess water from the leaves. Provide them with bright indirect lighting. They will live for several years and produce pups to become a clump. These can be removed to make a new plant if desired. Fertilize during the growing season with a dilute (half-strength or even less) liquid fertilizer. When the plant is getting ready to bloom the top leaves will turn bright red. There are many cultivars available that provide variable leaf or flower color. It is small and attractive and easy to grow houseplant or greenhouse subject. It can spend the summer months outdoors hanging from a tree or shady trellis, mimicking the way it grows in nature. Quick ID Grass-like leaves are green, entire, covered with silvery gray scales. Roots functioning as holdfasts (not anchored to soil). Flower is blue-violet on a short spike with red bracts. Insects, Diseases, and Other Plant Problems: This plant is not troubled by pests or diseases. More information on Tillandsia .

cultivars.name: T. ionantha 'Fuego
cultivars.note: fiery red color if in plenty of sunlight

cultivars.name: T. ionantha 'Guatemala
cultivars.note: spiky, bright green transitions to light pink/red, bloom purple spike with yellow flowers

cultivars.name: T. ionantha 'Mexican
cultivars.note: deep green transitions to red, purple bloom with yellow and white flowers

cultivars.name: T. ionantha 'Rubra
cultivars.note: soft and hard forms, soft is short, and hard is more vertical. Leaves are red.

Light: Dappled Sunlight (Shade through upper canopy all day)
Fruit Description: A subcylindrical capsule 0.5" long, seeds have feathery tufts of hair and are dispersed by wind.
Flower Description: The inflorescence is a very short terminal spike. A reduced panicle that looks spike-like with violet-purple petals and yellow stamens.
Leaf Description: Leaves are in a rosette, simple, linear-lanceolate, acute, bases wide and flattened, entire, succulent, medium green covered with absorbent gray scales, to 2.5 in; inner leaves flush red before flowering.
Stem Description: Stem is short, simple; roots few, wiry.
